featureAccess.eyebrow: More ways to use Libraries Global
featureAccess.accountNote: Use your existing account, or create one for free. Any extra access requirements are explained here.
featureAccess.teamTitle: Your next step with a Team
featureAccess.teamNote: These tools use a Team workspace. Set one up, or ask your organiser for an invitation to an existing Team.

networks.title: Sign in to manage your service or network
networks.lead: Connect your libraries and request the access you need to keep a service’s records up to date.

benefits.one: Confirm your affiliation with a library service or network.
benefits.two: Request management access across the libraries you look after.
benefits.three: Follow the progress of requests and see your approved scope.

networks.requirement: A free account lets you request affiliation. Service-management access is reviewed separately; paying for a plan does not grant it.

teams.title: Sign in to bring your Team together
teams.lead: Connect colleagues, organise membership and use tools built for library services.

benefits.one: Invite colleagues and manage Team membership.
benefits.two: Connect your service’s libraries with the right people.
benefits.three: Use Team tools, including widgets, with active access.

teams.requirement: Team membership and Library staff access are separate. Verification is required for staff editing; payment never grants that authority.
teams.memberTitle: Bring your service together with a Team

widgets.title: Sign in to put library data on your website
widgets.lead: Create maps, directories and charts that stay connected to published library records.

benefits.one: Reuse a selection of libraries across different formats.
benefits.two: Shape a map, directory or comparison for your website.
benefits.three: Preview drafts and manage publication from your workspace.

widgets.requirement: Widgets require active Team access. Editing and publication remain subject to your Team permissions.
widgets.memberTitle: Put library data on your website with Team

api.title: Sign in to connect your application
api.lead: Build with public library data through your Team’s API add-on.

benefits.one: Connect your own tools to published library records.
benefits.two: Manage API access within your authorised Team.
benefits.three: See request allowances and usage in one place.

api.requirement: The API is a separate paid add-on for Teams. Creating an account or buying a personal plan does not activate API access.
api.memberTitle: Connect your application with the Team API

claim.title: Sign in to claim your library
claim.lead: Work at a library? Keep its public record accurate at the source.
claim.action: Sign in to claim a library
claim.publicAction: Find your library in the index

benefits.one: Keep hours, services and accessibility information current.
benefits.two: Publish notices and connect an events feed.
benefits.three: Manage mobile routes and stops where your library offers them.

claim.requirement: Claiming and maintaining a library is free. A moderator checks your role and evidence before staff editing is enabled.

index.title: Sign in to improve a library record
index.lead: A small, sourced correction helps everyone who uses the index.

benefits.one: Find the library and check what is already recorded.
benefits.two: Add hours, photos, accessibility details or a reliable source.
benefits.three: Save a draft and follow your suggestion through review.

index.requirement: A free account is enough to suggest changes. Ordinary contributions are reviewed before publication; no paid plan is required.

add.title: Sign in to put a library on the map
add.lead: Know a library that is missing? Add what you know and help others find it.
add.action: Sign in to add a library

benefits.one: Start with its name, library type and a source.
benefits.two: Add its location, hours and services as you find them.
benefits.three: Save your draft and receive feedback from a reviewer.

add.requirement: Adding a library is free. Check for an existing record first; an editor reviews your submission before it goes live.

writing.title: Sign in to share a library story
writing.lead: Write for the Journal and discover how to help maintain Knowledge.

benefits.one: Propose a story about a library, a visit or a discovery.
benefits.two: Keep drafts and follow editorial feedback in one workspace.
benefits.three: Explore Knowledge and the roles that maintain its guides.

writing.requirement: Free accounts can propose Journal stories. Publishing Knowledge requires an editorial role, approved separately from membership.

roles.title: Sign in to find your contributor role
roles.lead: Help maintain guides, edit stories or review the community’s suggestions.

benefits.one: Choose a role that matches your experience and interests.
benefits.two: Explain the languages and topics you can help with.
benefits.three: Follow your application and any requests for more information.

roles.requirement: Contributor roles are reviewed using experience, contribution history and the role’s requirements. A paid membership does not buy approval.

atlasAnalysis.densityMethod: We divide an area's population by its size in square kilometres, including inland water. This gives an average for the whole area. Some neighbourhoods will have more people per square kilometre than others.
atlasAnalysis.densityCoverage: Country populations come from the World Bank. UK district estimates come from the Office for National Statistics (ONS). We add district totals from the same year to form county groups. These groups follow our directory's district boundaries, which can differ from ceremonial counties.

atlasAnalysis.reachMethod: We use mapped roads and paths to estimate journeys to the library, then count the people who live within that area. These figures estimate nearby residents, rather than library visits.

atlasAnalysis.reachUnsupported: Reach isn't available for this library yet. We support fixed-location libraries in England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland where routing and population data are available. Planned, temporarily closed and permanently closed libraries are excluded.
atlasAnalysis.reachAvailability: Explore walking and cycling journeys to libraries across the UK.
atlasAnalysis.reachAccessMessage: Pro and Team include Reach analysis. Library facts remain free.
atlasAnalysis.reachCountsExplanation: The 15-minute total includes everyone within 5 and 10 minutes. Don't add the rows together.

atlasAnalysis.reachSpeeds: We assume a walking speed of 5.1 km/h or 15 km/h on a hybrid bike.

0.a: Supporter and Pro use tax-inclusive GBP base prices. Stripe confirms the applicable tax, local currency and final recurring total before you pay. Team is billed yearly through Stripe, excluding VAT where stated.

1.a: Cancel renewal at any time through Membership & billing in Settings. Your settled membership stays available until the paid period ends. Refund requests follow the cancellation and refund policy and Stripe’s order terms; your statutory rights remain unchanged.

2.a: Create a Team online, choose seats and pay yearly through Stripe. Payment confirmation activates Team access and Pro for every seat. Your Organiser invites colleagues. Library claims and permission to edit records are optional and reviewed separately.

3.a: Detailed change history and Atlas CSV/GeoJSON exports of up to {supporter, number} libraries per download. Pro raises the cap to {pro, number} and adds population comparisons. Unfinished tools are marked Coming soon.

4.q: Can I use Apple Pay or Google Pay?
4.a: Stripe’s checkout shows payment methods supported for your device and location, including Apple Pay and Google Pay when available. Card payment is available. Libraries Global does not receive your full card details.

5.q: Does membership change my role or how my edits are reviewed?
5.a: No. Money never buys trust. Supporter and Pro do not award points, raise your tier, change your contributor role or skip review.

6.a: Every library record, with hours and services, search, the map and lists stay free for everyone, signed in or not. Contributing is free too.

atlasInsights.additional: Extending the threshold from {from} to {to} minutes includes an estimated {residents} additional residents.
atlasInsights.beyond: An estimated {residents} residents remain beyond {minutes} minutes from the selected libraries.
atlasInsights.bandExplanation: Each resident appears in one band. Bar lengths show the share of the reporting population, not the length of the time interval.
atlasInsights.cumulativeExplanation: Residents within each threshold. These counts accumulate, so they must not be added together. Select a time to update the map.
atlasInsights.rounding: Resident estimates are rounded for display. Rounded bands may differ slightly from the rounded total.
atlasInsights.incompleteDistribution: The travel-time distribution needs complete routing and population data. Missing residents cannot be assigned to a band.
atlasInsights.contextExplanation: Compare modelled coverage within {minutes} minutes across groups of areas in this nation.
atlasInsights.groupExplanation: Deciles 1–2 contain the most deprived fifth of areas nationally; 9–10 contain the least deprived fifth. Groups contain different numbers of residents. All bars run from 0 to 100%.
atlasInsights.coverageByGroup: Percentage of each group’s modelled population within reach
atlasInsights.gap: Modelled coverage differs by {points} percentage points between {high} (highest) and {low} (lowest).
atlasInsights.outsideShareExplanation: Share beyond reach uses all reporting-area residents beyond the chosen time, including unclassified areas, as its denominator.
atlasInsights.contextLimits: These are area-based relative indices. They do not describe every resident, establish causation or support direct comparisons between nations. Unknown classifications stay separate from known groups.
atlasInsights.simdLimits: Overall SIMD includes access to services. That overlap can affect this comparison; it does not provide an independent test of the relationship between deprivation and accessibility. Income and employment domains are not included here.
atlasInsights.intersectionMethod: Full source deprivation boundaries partition the reporting area in the population grid’s equal-area projection. We allocate each cell’s modelled residents by its intersecting area, then intersect each group with the union of library catchments. Conflicting classifications and uncovered areas remain unclassified.
atlasInsights.populationMismatch: Population uses the {year} modelled grid. Index editions and boundary years differ; this is a spatial comparison, not a same-year population survey.
atlasInsights.incompleteContext: Community comparisons need complete routing and population coverage. No group percentages are shown for this incomplete calculation.
atlasInsights.insufficientContext: The community calculation could not be reconciled within its data or processing limits. Group percentages are unavailable; the service reach result remains available.
atlasInsights.unavailableContext: A compatible analytical deprivation edition is not installed for this reporting area. A map overlay alone cannot provide this comparison.
atlasInsights.singleTimeDistribution: This result covers {minutes} minutes only. Distinct journey-time bands need all four times, so they are not shown for this calculation.

atlasDensity.method: Published library coordinates are counted in geographic cells. Density is the count divided by the spherical cell area, including water, multiplied by 100. Automatic detail changes cell size, while a fixed colour scale keeps rates comparable.
